text:
ana (cs): Heads-up — Customer Heartline (acct: heartline-prod) reporting p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~900ms on /v1/embeddings in US-W2 after last night's infra patch. Customer says it started ~2026-03-16 02:00 UTC. Tagging SRE + infra. sample req ids: r_0a1b2c3d, r_0a1b2c3e

deploy-bot: rollout completed: driver v525.40 -> v526.10 + GPU FW 1.2.3 applied to us-west-2 fleet at 2026-03-16T01:45Z

sarah (support): thanks @ana. Can we get a few full request IDs, model, and whether it's embeddings/rtp? Also any correlation with auth errors? Customer didn't change client.

ana (cs): sending two request IDs: r_0a1b2c3d (embeddings-text-32k), r_0a1b2c3e (chat-std). No auth errors, just tail latency. Customer says it affects ~10% of requests.

taylor (eng-sre): :eyes: interesting. Early suspicion: host IO stalls after the driver/fw rollout. Can infra run dmesg/journalctl on affected nodes and collect nvme SMART and iostat -x 1 10. Also capture top -H and pidstat during spike.

matt (eng-infra): agreed. We pushed a kernel backport (linux-6.6.12) last week as well; possible preempt path change. I'll correlate nodes for the two req ids and run `sudo journalctl -k --since '2026-03-16 00:30' | grep -i -E 'nvme|I/O|firmware|nvidia'`

kevin (eng-runtime): also check model routing — runtime may be falling back to a larger variant when a worker times out. Please dump /var/log/redwood/runtime/route-trace.log around the timestamps. Quick curl to fetch traces: `curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RED_TOKEN' https://internal-api/trace?r=r_0a1b2c3d`

sarah (support): customer supplied a small repro script. I ran it against us-west-2 and saw p95 ~820ms consistently for small batch=1. Attaching minimal output: `latency_samples: [120, 130, 150, 820, 900]`

matt (eng-infra): collected nvme stats from nodes serving those reqs — one node shows intermittent write latency spikes and `nvme_core: reset controller` entries. Filing quick mitigation: cordon node and force drain. Will surface node ids in convo.

taylor (eng-sre): mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain bad nodes 2) route Heartline to dedicated pool (temp) 3) rollback driver/firmware on a canary subset if we repro after drain. Also add temporary increase to routing fallback threshold to avoid larger-model fallback.

ana (cs): customer approved temporary routing to dedicated pool. Can we get ETA?

kevin (eng-runtime): On it — I'll open a canary pool and add a routing rule for `acct:heartline-prod` -> dedicated-usw2-small within 15m. Also adding extra KV cache warmup to reduce IO for embeddings.

deploy-bot: workflow: cordon/drain started on node ip 10.2.14.21 by matt at 2026-03-16T02:10Z

sarah (support): thanks team. Keep me posted and I'll update Heartline support channel. Next steps: collect dmesg + nvme logs, verify p95 improves after drain, decide rollback if not.
